title: Follow-ups from the backend-ibkr-conid-db-cache PR review (#384)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's full review of PR #384 (backend-ibkr-conid-db-cache), recorded here per CLAUDE.md's convention so they aren't lost once the PR merges. None of these blocked the accept -- the PR's own scope (DB-backed conid cache surviving a restart) was delivered correctly and completely, verified by mutation testing of both the concurrent-write-race swallow and the DB-cache-hit-skips-live-call claim, a clean scratch-DB migration upgrade/downgrade/upgrade round-trip, confirmation the migration is already applied to the real dev-container DB with the correct schema, and a session-lifecycle check confirming each DB-cache read/write opens and closes its own short-lived session rather than holding one open across the method.

checklist.step: `docs/architecture/Backend.md`'s description of `IBKRProvider.resolve_conid`'s caching (the paragraph beginning "`IBKRProvider.resolve_conid` caches each ticker's resolved conid... for 24h on the `IBKRProvider` instance itself") still describes the cache as purely in-memory/process-wide-singleton and doesn't mention the new `IBKRConidCacheORM`-backed, permanent, restart-surviving fallback cache this PR added. Update that paragraph (or add a short new subsection, matching the precedent `backend-cftc-cot-caching-scheduler` set by adding Backend.md's own §9 for an analogous DB-backed-cache addition) to describe the new DB-cache layer, its 'only successful resolutions, no TTL' semantics, and the `session_factory` injection pattern.

No test asserts that `app.api.dependencies._get_ibkr_provider_singleton()`'s production wiring actually passes `session_factory=SessionLocal` to the constructed `IBKRProvider` (e.g. `provider._session_factory is SessionLocal`) -- the new line is only exercised incidentally by existing singleton-construction tests (which is why it shows as 100% covered), not verified behaviorally. Add a small assertion so a future refactor that silently drops this wiring (re-introducing the pre-this-PR behavior of never checking the DB cache in production) would be caught.

The task's own checklist item 1 suggested the new cache table could additionally persist 'the disambiguating exchange/description if useful for debugging a wrong resolution later', but the final schema (`ticker`, `conid`, `resolved_at`) omits it, and none of the three recorded `decisions` entries explain why that optional field was left out. Either add a `decisions` entry recording that this was considered and deliberately scoped out (and why), or add the column if it's judged worth having for debugging a future wrong-resolution report.
